_notes: What a pastor can do with money that is not owed (DESIGN §8.2, playtesting). 'once' spends apply their effects when bought; 'fund' spends stand, draw their upkeep from cash each week and apply their weekly effects while the cash lasts. Conditions use the ordinary schema; 'parish' conditions read the current parish. The investment is engine-side (systems/spending.ts, endowment). Standing programs (marketing, the school, the staff, formation, online) are funds too: they run every week until wound up and can be set up again; besides `weekly` effects a fund may carry `pull` (attendance target while it stands), `growth` (households a year, as a share), `school` (school condition a week), `groups` (vitality a week to every supported group), `relief` (a block of the week the staff carry), and `collections` (a share on every collection). Chapel and monastery spends (playtesting): a spend may carry `house` so its {house} reads as the diocese's house of that charism; 'house' conditions check the diocese has one.

spends.label: A tuition assistance fund
spends.blurb: Families who cannot pay the school's tuition, paid for by the parish. Enrollment steadies and the school stops being a thing only the comfortable can use.

spends.label: A medical assistance fund
spends.blurb: Prescriptions, a clinic visit, the bill that would have ended a family. Run through the parish nurse or the St. Vincent de Paul conference, quietly.

spends.label: A fund for the poor
spends.blurb: Rent, groceries, a bus ticket home. The pastor's discretionary fund made large enough to matter, and the people who come to the door know it.

spends.label: A parish mission
spends.blurb: A week of preaching by a visiting order, every evening, with confessions until the church empties. The parish talks about it for a year.

spends.label: A feast-day festival
spends.blurb: Three nights on the lot: food, a band, a procession, the whole neighborhood. The groups run the booths and remember that they are a parish.

spends.label: Expand the church
spends.blurb: A transept, a wider nave, a hundred more seats and a narthex people can gather in. Two years of dust, and a building that fits the parish it has become.

spends.label: Build a parish hall
spends.blurb: A hall the parish has never had, or one that holds the parish it now is. Every group in the parish will want Tuesday night in it.

spends.label: An adoration chapel
spends.blurb: A room with a door that locks, a monstrance, and a schedule of people who come at three in the morning. Nothing else in the parish will change it as much.

spends.label: Hire a youth minister
spends.blurb: A salary the parish has never paid, for the young people it has been losing. The groups feel it first.

spends.label: Fund the music
spends.blurb: A paid cantor, a repaired organ, a choir that rehearses. The Mass sounds like somebody meant it.

spends.label: Make the parish known
spends.blurb: A sign that can be read from the road, a bulletin people keep, the website, the welcome desk, a man at the diocesan paper who knows your name. Families from two towns over start to register.

spends.label: Raise the school
spends.blurb: Teachers paid nearer what the public schools pay, a reading specialist, the science room, the principal's list. Enrollment follows quality, slowly, and the diocese notices a school that is not a problem.

spends.label: Pay the staff properly
spends.blurb: A raise, a Christmas bonus, health insurance that covers something. The secretary stops looking, the DRE stays, and the office runs without you in it.

spends.label: Adult formation
spends.blurb: A speaker a month, a Bible study that does not die in Lent, a paid coordinator. The people who come become the people who run things.

spends.label: The parish online
spends.blurb: The Mass streamed, the bulletin emailed, the giving done by phone. The homebound see you; the young give from the car.

spends.label: Restore the chapel
spends.blurb: The plaster patched and painted, the windows releaded, a proper altar with a reredos behind it, a lamp that burns. A room people come into on purpose, and the first thing a visitor sees that says the parish is loved.

spends.label: Perpetual adoration
spends.blurb: Someone before the monstrance every hour of the week: a sign-up sheet, a coordinator, the three a.m. slots filled by the same four people for years. The parish's prayer, kept going, and the thing people from other parishes drive over for.

spends.label: Join forces with {house}
spends.blurb: A standing arrangement with {house}: their guesthouse for your retreats and your people at their Sunday Mass; their name in your bulletin and yours in their prayers; a door that opens when you knock. It costs a gift to their building fund and a Sunday a year.

spends.label: A stipend to {house}
spends.blurb: Mass stipends and a monthly cheque to {house}, and the parish's intentions read at their Office every morning. Nothing visible happens, which is the point; the people know, and something in the parish is steadier for it.

spends.label: A confessor from {house}
spends.blurb: A friar from {house} in your confessional on Saturdays and the feasts, and in your pulpit when you are away, for a stipend and lunch. The line moves, the people have a second face to tell things to, and your week gets a block back.
